description: Unauthorized Data Lake Access via Misconfigured S3 Bucket Attackers could exploit misconfigured bucket policies, overly permissive IAM roles, or Lake Formation permission gaps to access sensitive data in the S3 data lake. This could happen through direct S3 API calls or by assuming compromised IAM roles. An attacker discovers a misconfigured bucket policy that allows authenticated AWS users to list and read objects. They could then use stolen credentials or a compromised role to access and exfiltrate sensitive data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict S3 bucket policies and block public access

description: Real-time Data Processing Pipeline Injection Attackers could inject malformed or malicious data into the ingestion pipeline, potentially causing processing errors, buffer overflows, or SQL injection in downstream systems. Unsanitized data could propagate through the pipeline and affect multiple components. An attacker injects malicious data through the Kinesis stream that contains SQL injection payloads. When this data is processed by Lambda and written to Redshift, it could execute unauthorized queries.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement data validation and sanitization

description: API Gateway Security Vulnerabilities Attackers could exploit weak API security controls to gain unauthorized access, perform credential stuffing attacks, or launch DoS attacks against the API endpoints. An attacker performs a credential stuffing attack against the API endpoints, attempting to gain unauthorized access to the analytics platform using compromised credentials from other breaches.
references: recommendation: Implement comprehensive API security controls

description: Insufficient Monitoring and Incident Detection Without proper monitoring and logging, attackers could perform reconnaissance, gain unauthorized access, or exfiltrate data without detection. System misuse or performance issues might also go unnoticed. An attacker gains access to the system through compromised credentials and slowly exfiltrates data over time. Without proper monitoring, this activity goes undetected for months.
references: owaspTop10: A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

description: Data Privacy and PII Exposure PII and sensitive data could be inadvertently exposed through analytics outputs, machine learning model predictions, or search results. This could occur due to insufficient data sanitization or access controls. An analyst uses QuickSight to create a dashboard that accidentally exposes customer PII. The dashboard is then shared with unauthorized users or exported to external systems.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories
recommendation: Enable data discovery and monitoring
